summary: Runners mostly describe the Superblast 2 as a firm, stable and very durable trainer for long runs and daily miles, with many reporting very long wear. A break-in of many miles is common, and some never warm to the stiff, heavy feel at slow paces.

Most runners find the Boston 12 firm and very durable, with a grippy outsole that lasts many hundreds of kilometres. It suits tempo and faster running better than easy days, and many need a break-in period. The main complaint is heel slip and poor lockdown from the upper and laces.

Most runners find the Megablast bouncy, responsive and very durable, with plenty of life left after hundreds of miles and use as an all-round trainer. The narrow, low toe box is the main complaint, causing blisters, especially on the pinky toes, and lockdown is hard for some.

Runners mostly find the Adizero EVO SL light, bouncy and fun at faster paces, and many get long wear from it. Instability is the main complaint, with ankle soreness and a wobbly feel at slow paces or on longer runs. It suits workouts and shorter runs better than long easy miles.

Most runners find the Adios Pro 3 fast and bouncy, with a midsole and outsole that last for hundreds of miles. The upper and laces are the main complaint, with blisters, lace bite and heel rubbing common, and some find it wobbly. Works best for runners who can get the lockdown right.

Most runners find the Vomero Plus very plush and durable, a soft, bouncy shoe for easy and long runs. The main complaints are instability, especially on uneven ground or turns, and weight that some notice after 6 to 8 km. A few find the fit narrow.

Most runners find the Novablast 5 soft, bouncy and comfortable, with a roomy, breathable upper. The main complaint is that the cushioning goes flat sooner than expected, often somewhere between 250 and 400 km, though a few get far more. Some find it less stable than the Novablast 4.

Most runners describe the Adios Pro 4 as soft, bouncy and fast, with a more comfortable upper than the Adios Pro 3. Many go half a size up because the toe box runs narrow, and some get heel blisters or find it less stable. Mainly used for races and long runs.

Runners mostly find the Superblast 3 softer and bouncier than the Superblast 2, a comfortable shoe for easy and long runs that many still find stable. Some find it too soft or unstable, especially on turns or at faster paces, and a few report wear sooner than expected.

Many runners like the Rebel v4's roomy, comfortable upper and light, soft feel for easy and tempo runs. The main complaint is that the midsole goes flat early, often around 200 to 250 miles, and some find it lacks bounce, especially next to earlier Rebels.

Many runners find the Adizero SL2 soft, bouncy and responsive, softer than the original SL. The main drawback is a narrow, tight midfoot that causes blisters and hot spots for many, and several go up half a size. Some keep it to shorter daily runs.

Most runners find the Invincible 3 plush and bouncy, good for easy and long runs. Heel slip is the main complaint, often needing heel-lock lacing and easing with wear for some, and many also find it heavy or a bit unstable. A few find it firmer than earlier versions.

Runners mostly find the Hyperion Tempo light, fast and firm, with good ground feel and stability. It is best loved for tempo runs, intervals and shorter races, while some find it too thin or unforgiving for slow or very long runs. Many report it lasting several hundred miles.

Runners mostly find the Dynafish XiaoNian light, stable and bouncy, a versatile trainer from easy to tempo runs that holds up well, with several reporting around 1,000 km. The stock laces, thin insole and average upper draw some criticism, and a few get sore knees or feet.

Runners mostly find the Pegasus 39 a durable, comfortable everyday trainer, with an upper that fits well and an outsole that often passes 400 miles. The ride leans firm, and some find it clunky at slow paces or tiring past 10 km. A few find it narrow.

Most runners call the Adizero SL firm but durable, with a grippy outsole that lasts through hundreds of miles. Those who like a firmer ride enjoy it as a versatile daily trainer, while others find it too harsh for easy days or long runs past about 10 km. Some say it softens a little with miles.

Most runners find the Mach 6 light, responsive and fun for daily and tempo runs, and many get several hundred kilometres from it. A narrow fit is the main complaint, with many buying the wide version or sizing up, and a few report the foam or outsole wearing out early.

Runners mostly find the Vaporfly 3 fast, light and comfortable, with a roomier forefoot and softer ride than the Vaporfly 2. Complaints are scattered: some get arch pain or blisters, find it less stable, or see the outsole and foam wear sooner than expected. A race-day shoe.

Runners mostly find the Endorphin Speed 4 comfortable, snappy and fast, with a rocker that comes alive at faster paces. The narrow fit is the main complaint, causing toe pressure for several. Some find it firm or clunky at easy paces and less suited to the longest runs.

Most runners call the Vaporfly NEXT% 2 very fast and light, best for races from the 5K to the half marathon. Fit is a recurring problem, with narrow or tight feel, heel slip and blisters for some, and several see the foam and outsole wear quickly. Some find it hard on the calves or too aggressive for a marathon.

Most runners find the PUMA Deviate Nitro Elite 3 fast, bouncy and comfortable, with many setting PBs from 5K to marathon in it and several calling it stable and durable. The main downsides are a narrow fit, and a few find the heel unstable or the foam fading after a while. It suits narrower feet best.

Most runners love the PUMA MagMax Nitro as a bouncy, protective, durable shoe for easy miles and long runs, with a wide stable base and some getting several hundred miles from a pair. The main downside is weight, which feels clunky when picking up the pace. A few get blisters on the ball of the foot or find the midfoot tight.

Most runners find the Salomon Genesis a durable, comfortable all-round trail shoe, trusted for long technical days and ultras, with a snug upper that many say fits well. The main downsides are a narrow forefoot for some, and a few report heel slip or poor wet grip. A couple find the cushioning too little for very long races.

Runners split on the New Balance FuelCell SuperComp Trainer v2. Many like its soft, comfortable, bouncy ride for easy and long runs, and some report several hundred miles of use. The most common complaint is that it wears out fast, with outsole wear and flattening foam, and some find it too soft, a little heavy and clunky at pace.

Most runners find the PUMA Deviate Pure Nitro a comfortable, stable, versatile daily trainer with a roomy upper, though the foam is on the firm side and some wish for more bounce. A few say it softens after break-in. Some find the toe box tight, and a couple report upper or outsole wear.

Most runners love the Brooks Cascadia 19 as a comfortable, well-cushioned, grippy trail shoe, with many wide-footed runners and ultra runners happy in it. It is softer and plusher than earlier versions, which a few longtime fans dislike. A few mention slow drying, wet-rock grip or a tight fit.

Most runners find the PUMA Fast-R Nitro Elite 3 very light and fast, with many reporting PBs from 5K up to the marathon. The main downside is a narrow, snug fit. Several find it punishing on the calves or less comfortable past half distance, and a few note instability at the heel.

Most runners love the Li-Ning Red Hare 9 Ultra as a bouncy, well-cushioned, fun shoe for long runs and daily miles, and several report it holding up for hundreds of miles. The main downsides are a tight fit for some and a lack of stability that suits some runners less.

Runners split on the Nike Pegasus Trail 5. Many find it comfortable and a good fit for road-to-trail and moderate trails, including for wide feet. The most common complaint is a narrow upper that hurts the top of the foot for some, and several report heel slip, firm or dead foam, early wear, or poor stability on technical ground.

Runners praise the New Balance Fresh Foam X Hierro v9 for plush cushioning, good grip and comfort on easy trails and long days. The main downside is instability, with many reporting the foot rolling inward or the shoe feeling tippy at its high stack. A few get blisters from the toe cap, and some see early wear.

Most runners like the PUMA Velocity Nitro 4 as a responsive, durable daily trainer that handles easy runs and can pick up the pace, with several reporting hundreds of kilometres of use. The main complaint is a narrow, snug fit, especially through the midfoot, though some find the upper wide enough.

Most runners use the adidas Adizero Takumi Sen 10 as a light, fast shoe for intervals, tempo runs and 5K to 10K racing, with several setting PBs in it. The main downside is a narrow, snug race fit, and the firm ride and instability make it less suited to slow or long runs, particularly for lighter runners.

Runners split on the adidas Hyperboost Edge. Many like its bouncy, cushioned midsole and a comfortable ride for easy and long runs. The upper draws the most complaints, with several finding it hot, poorly breathable or tight, and a few report poor lockdown or the shoe going dead early.

Many runners find the Nike Pegasus Premium bouncy and comfortable for easy and long runs, with a premium feel. The main complaint is weight, which several say limits it on inclines and faster paces. Some find it unstable or awkward to run in, and a few report early wear or a poor experience.

Most runners find the adidas Adizero Adios 8 a light, fast, low-stack shoe with good ground feel, well suited to speed work and daily training. Many call it durable and breathable, and some say it fits wider than earlier versions. It has little stability, and a few find it slappy, firm or dead underfoot.

Most runners find the adidas Adizero Adios Pro 5 comfortable and stable, with a roomy toe box and good upper, and a smoother, more stable ride than the Pro 4. Some say it feels more like a super trainer, with firmer foam and modest snap. Durability concerns and a narrow fit for some are the main downsides.

Most runners find the Altra Timp 5 comfortable and protective, with strong traction and a fit many prefer to other Altras, especially for wide midfeet. The main downside is durability, with several reporting upper blowouts or tread wear. Some find it stiff, narrower than the Lone Peak or a little unstable.

Most runners find the ASICS Magic Speed 4 light, bouncy and versatile, from long runs and tempos to races up to the half marathon, with several setting PBs in it. A few find it a touch heavy for speed work, harsh on the calves or legs, or underwhelming at threshold. Fit complaints are scattered.

Runners praise the ASICS Gel Trabuco 13 for grip and a comfortable, stable feel on technical trails. The main downside is durability, with many reporting the upper tearing or separating within a few hundred kilometres, sometimes much sooner. Some also find the ride firm and hard on the legs.

Most runners find the New Balance FuelCell SuperComp Elite v4 bouncy, comfortable and stable, with a roomy toe box that suits wider feet, and good for long road runs and marathons. The main downsides are weight and some heel slip or rubbing. A few find the low drop and short tongue awkward.

Most runners love the Saucony Kinvara Pro as a stable, comfortable, peppy shoe for long runs and marathon training, and it also works for uptempo efforts. A few find it heavy on longer runs, and one reports the exposed outsole wearing quickly. A small number were underwhelmed.

Most runners find the On Cloudeclipse comfortable, stable and long-lasting, with a soft yet snappy ride that works for easy and daily runs. The most repeated complaint is squeaking, which several owners noticed early on. One runner found the cushioning went hard well before the shoe was worn out.

Most runners rate the PUMA Magnify Nitro 2 as a cushioned, durable daily and long-run shoe with a tough, grippy outsole. The downsides are that it feels bulky or firm to some, and it is not suited to fast running. A couple of runners saw wear or a fading pop with high mileage.

Runners who race long trail distances love the Salomon S/Lab Genesis for its precise, secure fit, grip and stability on technical terrain. Many use it for 50 km up to 100-mile races and rate it well above the regular Genesis. No real complaints came up, apart from a note that it suits some foot shapes better than others.

Most runners find the Saucony Triumph 24 a light, soft yet bouncy daily trainer with a comfortable fit and good energy return. Several say it feels livelier than earlier Triumph versions and works for long runs and picking up the pace. One runner found it too soft and roomy around the ankle.

Most runners like the ASICS Glideride Max as a comfortable, well-cushioned daily trainer that handles easy and long runs and can still pick up the pace. Some find it more plain than exciting. A couple worry about outsole wear, and one pair gave out after a few hundred miles.

Runners mostly find the ASICS Trabuco 14 comfortable, especially for gravel and light to moderate trail. The main drawback is that it rides firmer and stiffer than some expected, and a few found it less bouncy than road shoes. Durability reports are mixed, including midsole and exposed foam damage.

Most runners like the Brooks Cascadia Elite as a stable, protective trail shoe with soft, responsive foam, used for long runs and ultras. Fit is the common sticking point, with some finding the forefoot too wide or causing discomfort. A few found the foam too soft or squirrelly.

Most runners like the New Balance Fresh Foam X 880 v14 for its comfortable, roomy fit and as a dependable daily and long-run trainer. The ride is simple and mid-cushioned, with some finding the foam lacks return. Durability varies, with some pairs lasting a long time and one feeling worn out much sooner.

Many runners find the New Balance FuelCell Propel v4 a comfortable, durable and good-value daily trainer with some pop from its plate. Several had problems, though: heel slip, foam that felt dead or broke down, and a warm upper. Opinions split, so it suits some runners far better than others.

Most runners find the PUMA ForeverRun Nitro a comfortable, cushioned and mildly stable daily trainer that suits easy and recovery runs. The main downside is durability, with the foam dying or glue and toe box wearing out for some. Heel slip and running small came up in a couple of reviews.

Most runners find the Salomon Ultra Glide 2 comfortable, with a secure heel hold and enough cushion for roads and many trails. Durability is the main complaint, as the midsole went flat or delaminated for several runners. Grip in mud was also called weak by some.

Runners mostly see the adidas Ultraboost Light as a stable casual, walking and travel shoe rather than a running shoe. Several found it heavy, firm or poorly suited to running, though a few use it for short daily runs. Some have put many miles on it.

Most runners love the Altra Lone Peak 9 for its roomy, comfortable toe box and light, breathable feel on trails. The main complaints are that the cushioning breaks down or feels firm, and durability varies from heavy wear to very long life. Sizing and quality drew complaints from a couple of runners.

Most runners find the Altra Olympus 275 very comfortable and well cushioned, with strong grip and a tough upper for long technical trail days. Fit comes with a few quirks, such as a wide shape and a heel that folds down. Exposed foam wear and some foot slide or sores were each mentioned.

Most runners like the Brooks Glycerin 22 as a comfortable, responsive road shoe, especially for long runs. The main drawback is fit, with one runner finding the toe box narrower than before. A couple noted it breathes less well or absorbs shock less than other Brooks shoes.

Most runners find the HOKA Clifton 10 soft, comfortable and good for easy and long runs, with several getting plenty of miles from it. It is not a fast shoe. A few who loved the Clifton 9 found the 10 firmer, clunky or wobbly, and one found it underwhelming for running.

Most runners find the New Balance Fresh Foam X Balos very soft, bouncy and fun, with a rockered ride and a snug, sock-like upper. It works for easy and long runs, and many say it holds up well. A few note it is too soft for harder workouts and one thought it pricey.

Runners are split on the New Balance FuelCell Rebel v5. Some like its roomy, comfortable fit and lively, cushioned ride for daily and longer runs. Others found it too soft for speed work, or felt the foam went flat well before the shoe was worn out.

Many runners find the Nike Pegasus 41 a reliable, comfortable and very durable daily shoe, with several logging a lot of miles in it. Fit is the main split, as some find the toe box roomy while others find the forefoot too narrow. A few found it heavy, lackluster or unresponsive.

Most runners love the On Cloudboom Strike as a fast, breathable race shoe with strong energy return and a secure feel. The main downsides are fit and comfort problems, with several getting blisters, heel lift or a hard heel cup. Some found it stable while one found it not stable, so it may suit midfoot strikers best.

Most runners love the Saucony Hurricane 25 as a stable, well-cushioned and comfortable shoe for easy, recovery and long runs. The main complaint is fit, with a few finding the toe box too narrow or pressing on the big toe. One runner got arch and shin pain after moving up from the previous version.

Runners find the Speedgoat 6 firm and stiff, with solid grip and a stable platform on rocky, technical trails. The main complaint is durability, with many reporting worn lugs, packed-out foam or upper damage early. Blisters, a short tongue and a narrow toe box also come up, though some get several hundred trouble-free kilometers.

Most runners find the Alphafly 3 comfortable, bouncy and stable, praised for racing and long efforts, with a roomy toe box and good heel hold. Downsides are noise that many notice and foam some feel loses its pop within a few hundred miles, though others report much longer life. It can feel clunky at slow paces.

Runners mostly like the Boston 13 as a stable, firm tempo and everyday shoe with a better upper than the 12 and secure lockdown. Firmness is the most common caveat, and some find it stiff or jarring at first. A tapered, narrow toe box bothers a fair number of runners, and the laces are often called short.

Runners describe the 1080 v13 as very soft and plush, loved for easy, recovery and slow long runs. The softness is also the main drawback: some find it mushy, unstable or short on energy return at faster paces. Durability is mostly good, though a few report early wear, and some find the toe box snug.

Many runners find the Vomero 18 a comfortable, well-cushioned and durable trainer for easy and long runs, with several reporting 500 miles or more. Weight is the clearest downside, with some calling it heavy and clunky, and it runs warm. A narrow fit troubles wider feet.

Runners describe the Azura as a firm, stable, light shoe that many use as a versatile do-it-all trainer, fast enough for tempo and workable for long runs. Firmness is the most common caveat: some find it very firm or harsh, though several say it softens with use. A few find the forefoot narrow.

Runners describe the Endorphin Elite 2 as a very soft, bouncy and fast racing shoe, with an upper many find among the most comfortable of any super shoe. The main drawback is instability, with several noting a wobbly feel at slow speeds or in corners. The tapered toe area brings pinky-toe blisters for some.

The Glycerin Max is plush yet surprisingly lively, and runners like it for easy, recovery and long runs. Arch and heel blisters are the most frequent complaint, with some getting them repeatedly or returning the shoe. Weight is the other common downside, and the upper runs warm.

The Bondi 8 is a heavily cushioned shoe that runners find soft and protective, and some run hundreds of kilometers in it. Narrow fit is the biggest complaint, even in the Wide version, along with arch pain and blisters. It is also often called heavy.

Runners find the Endorphin Pro 4 a comfortable, roomy and stable plated shoe that works for racing from 5K to the marathon. Many rate it below the Pro 3 for energy return at faster paces. A few report a loose heel or upper, and some saw the upper wear early.

Runners describe the Neo Zen as a soft, bouncy and fun daily trainer, and many report foam that stays lively for several hundred kilometers. The softness makes it feel unstable for some, and it turns mushy at faster paces. The sock-like upper divides opinion, with loose heels and stretch noted by a few.

Runners describe the Zegama 2 as a cushioned, grippy trail shoe that many find comfortable and durable over long distances. Stability is split: some call it very stable while others roll ankles in it. It is also described as heavy or bulky, and some get heel slip or collar rubbing.

Runners mostly like the Zoom Fly 6 as a comfortable, responsive tempo and workout shoe with a no-fuss upper, and several run many hundreds of kilometers in it. Some find it firm or stiff, especially for long runs, and a few say it lost its pop after a few hundred miles. A few get blisters.

The Mach X 2 is a light, springy shoe that most runners enjoy for tempo and long runs. The main problem is the heel and ankle collar, which gives heel slip and Achilles blisters to a good share of wearers, though others have no issues. A few mention outsole wear.

Runners describe the Aero Glide 3 as a light, bouncy daily trainer that many find versatile from easy to tempo paces, with several reporting 350 to 500 miles of use. Fit is the main variable: some find the midfoot narrow, while others find it roomy or long and size down.

The Cloudsurfer 7 is a very comfortable, light shoe that runners like for easy, recovery and daily runs, with a wide toe box and easy rocker. The most repeated complaint is squeaking, which many report appearing within weeks. Some find it best kept to slower or shorter runs.

The Pegasus Plus is a light, lively shoe with a comfortable, secure upper, and most runners enjoy it for tempo work and fast daily runs. Some find the fit snug and tapered, and a few feel it is not versatile for longer runs or does not stand out against rivals.

Runners describe the Endorphin Speed 5 as a firm, stable and light shoe that works for tempo and speed sessions, and some use it for everything. Reactions are lukewarm, with several calling it flat, dull or harsh, and firmness is the most common note. A few get heel slip or chafing.

Runners describe the Adios 9 as a light, low-stack, fast shoe with a comfortable sock-like upper and a durable outsole, popular for track sessions, intervals and shorter races. Heavy use can be hard on the knees and legs, so it is less suited to everyday long mileage. A few get heel blisters.

Runners find the Agravic Speed Ultra fast on smooth, non-technical trails and it gives a strong, propulsive ride. The dominant complaint is blisters, especially under the arches and at the heel, often blamed on a stiff upper. It is also unstable on rocky or technical terrain, and some struggle with lockdown.

Runners describe the Ultrafly as a stable, roomy trail shoe that many find comfortable and durable, best on smooth to moderate trails and groomed paths. Its stiff plate and firmness bother some, and a few call it heavy. Technical terrain is a weak spot, and a few see outsole or upper wear.

Most runners find the HOKA Speedgoat 7 comfortable, with a roomy fit that works for long, hilly runs, and a few say it feels stable and has held up for hundreds of kilometres. The main complaint is the upper failing early, with holes, ripped toe overlays and split stitching.

Most runners find the On Cloudmonster Hyper very comfortable, with a roomy upper and a springy ride that shines at faster paces and works as a daily trainer. A few got blisters or heel pain, and a couple found it heavy or clunky. Several say it is best bought on sale.

Most runners enjoy the ASICS Sonicblast as a lively, peppy shoe for tempo, threshold and interval work, and some wear it daily. A few found it too stiff and dead, and a couple reported poor durability or little grip.

Most runners rate the PUMA Deviate Nitro Elite 4 highly as a stable, fast racing shoe that also handles long runs and key workouts. Complaints are scattered, with a few preferring the Elite 3 and a couple of narrow-footed runners finding it roomy.

Most runners find the adidas Supernova Rise 2 a comfortable, durable everyday trainer that also works well for walking, and many mention buying it on sale. Some found the midsole or upper wearing out, and a few felt it firm or flat for faster running.

Most runners praise the Nike Vomero Premium for its very plush, joint-friendly cushioning on long and easy runs. The main downsides are its weight and a tall, soft stack that feels unstable to some, especially at first.

Most runners find the Nike Wildhorse 8 a comfortable, durable trail shoe that copes with long runs, ultras and mixed terrain, with a roomy toe box and good traction. Downsides are scattered: it is a bit heavy, and some find the foam soft or mushy and a little unstable on descents.

Most runners find the HOKA Skyward X comfortable and very durable, with a plush, bouncy ride for easy long runs and tempos, and many report hundreds of miles of wear. The main concern is the plate, which cracked for a couple of runners, and a few find it narrow.

Most runners like the PUMA MagMax Nitro 2 for its roomy, comfortable fit, which many say is much better than the original, and for easy and recovery runs. The main downside is a firm, dense foam with less bounce than some hoped. Heavier runners are often happy with it.

Most runners enjoy the adidas Adizero Takumi Sen 11 as a fast, snappy shoe for track, 5K and 10K efforts, with a soft upper and good energy return. The main downsides are a narrow fit and, for some, a lack of stability.

Runners are mixed on it. Many like the Agravic SL's bouncy, quick ride on less technical trails, but the most common complaint is instability, with ankles rolling for several runners. Fit is a second issue, with some finding the toe box narrow or the sizing off. It suits non-technical trails best.

Most runners rate the ASICS Metaspeed Sky Paris as a fast, light race shoe, and several ran marathon PRs in it. Downsides are a firm, unforgiving ride that feels flat at slower paces, and fit issues for some, including blisters, a baggy upper or tight toes.

Most runners like the HOKA Rocket X 3 as a stable, versatile racer for long runs, workouts and marathons that is not too aggressive. Complaints are minor and scattered: a few find the foam not especially fun or responsive, one had heel slip and one found it unstable.

Most runners love the HOKA Tecton X 3 as a plated trail shoe for long distances and ultras, with a protective, cushioned feel and a roomy toe box. The main downsides are instability for some and weaker suitability for technical terrain.

Most runners find the Nike ACG Zegama Trail comfortable and stable, with good lockdown and cushioning on rocky terrain and long distances. Downsides are scattered: a few found the tall, soft stack insecure, and individual reviews mention durability, heat and rock plate discomfort.

Most runners love the adidas Adizero Prime X 2 Strung as a bouncy, fast shoe for tempo work, long runs and racing. The main downsides are durability, with the plate breaking for a couple of runners and the outsole wearing fast, plus weight and instability for some. It suits runners with good balance.

Most runners find the ASICS Gel Trabuco 12 comfortable and reliable on mixed trails, with good grip and breathability. Downsides are a dull, low-energy ride, some instability on technical ground, and an upper that can give out before the outsole.

Most runners like the New Balance FuelCell SuperComp Trainer v3 as a responsive, stable and protective trainer for long runs and tempos, with an upper that several find more comfortable than the v2's. Complaints are scattered, such as a firm feel, foam going dead after high mileage, and a couple preferring other shoes.

Most runners find the Salomon Aero Glide 3 GRVL comfortable, grippy and cushioned, working on gravel and as a road trainer for long runs. A few found it firm at first, and individual reviews mention a hot or narrow upper and an outsole peeling.

Runners give mixed to positive reviews. Many like the ASICS Gel Nimbus 27 as a soft, stable max-cushion shoe for easy and recovery runs, while some find it too squishy, heavy or hard on the calves, and a few got blisters or heel slip.
Runners' reviews are split. Some like the Mizuno Neo Zen 2 as a stable, bouncy daily shoe, but several Neo Zen 1 fans find it firmer, narrower and less bouncy than the original.
Runners find it comfortable and stable for easy miles and walking, but several call it firm or dull, and it feels heavy once the pace picks up.
Runners mostly find it stable and well cushioned on long trail and groomed runs, but a few got heel, calf or Achilles pain, and several say it runs small.
Runners mostly find it fast and bouncy at race and threshold paces, with several calling it stable enough to race in. A few found it less comfortable at easy paces or on longer runs.
Runners mostly find it soft, cushioned and enjoyable for easy and long runs, with several calling it a long-run shoe.
Runners mostly like it as a durable do-it-all trainer, from easy miles to tempo and speed work, with good grip.
Runners are mixed. Several report it wearing out early, with soles splitting or fabric wearing through, and a couple found it too soft for a trail shoe.
Runners mostly find it light, bouncy and stable, with a fast feel and little break-in. A couple note the upper is less breathable or plasticky.
Runners praise its stable, secure fit, but opinions split on the ride, with several finding it stiff or awkward at pace and a few loving it for long runs.
Runners like the roomy toe box and cushioning, even on long trail runs, but the added heel pillow put off several.
Runners mostly find it a fast, bouncy race shoe that fits true to size and handles hard intervals well, though it is less good at slow paces.
Runners mostly find it comfortable, soft and springy, and fun from easy runs to tempo.
Runners mostly find it plush and comfortable, and softer than the Bondi 8. A few had problems with stability, fit or firmness.
Runners mostly find it bouncy and fun at faster paces, and several say it is stable for a race shoe. A few found it too soft or tiring over longer efforts.
Runners find it light, springy and best at faster paces, but several say the midfoot is narrow and the heel unstable, especially for heel strikers.
Runners mostly find it very soft and cushioned for easy and long runs. A few had fit problems such as blisters or numb toes.
Runners are positive across the board, describing a firmer-side, protective trainer that keeps the legs fresh.
Runners mostly find it comfortable and cushioned, though opinions differ on how propulsive it is, with some feeling a snappy toe-off and others a fairly traditional ride.
Runners mostly like it, especially for long runs. The sock-like upper takes some getting used to, and a few needed to size up or dial in lockdown.
Runners mostly like it as a comfortable trainer, though several find the ride flat or dead.
Runners praise it as a light, grippy, minimally cushioned trail shoe, but durability is split: several had outsoles crack or fail early while others got long wear.
Runners mostly use it for ultras and long trail days with good results, but some find it narrow or short.
Runners like it as a stable, comfortable trail shoe that does well on descents, but fit is a recurring problem, with some finding it too narrow or tight.
Runners mostly find it very plush and comfortable for long trail days and ultras. A few had trouble with lockdown or fit, or didn't get on with it.
Runners say it feels stable thanks to its low stack, but the main complaint is lugs tearing or wearing off early, reported by several. Some still love it.
Runners mostly love it as a fast, protective racer with a bouncy ride, with a couple running marathon PRs. A few found it narrow or wobbly.
Runners like the plush, soft cushioning, but several find the toe box tight or tapered, and a couple call it heavy and warm.
Runners mostly find it a comfortable stability shoe that rides much like the original, but several note a snugger, narrower fit than the first version.
Runners mostly like it as a cushioned, durable shoe for easy and long runs, with good wet grip. A couple found it unstable or clunky.
Runners find the Ultraboost 5X plush and comfortable, with a good midsole for easy days. The main problem is the upper, which is hard to lock down, so heel slip and sliding feet come up repeatedly.

Runners mostly like the Experience Flow 2's soft, responsive foam and see it as a clear step up from the first Flow. A few find it borderline too soft, too low on cushion for a big runner, or flat after about 300 km.
Runners agree the VIA Olympus rides very firm. Some like that along with the wide toe box, while others find it stiff, brick-like and painful on long runs.
Runners find the Dynablast 5 comfortable, cushioned and stable, and several see it as a worthy successor to the Novablast 3. It works as a dependable everyday trainer.
Runners find the Hyperion 2 light, springy and fast, well suited to tempo work and speed sessions up to marathon pace. It rides firm, so it is not a soft easy-day shoe.
Runners find the Hyperion Max 3 soft, cushioned and stable for easy and long runs, with some bounce left for faster work. It is a bit heavy, and one finds it tight beyond 5 to 7 miles.
Runners see speed and a good midsole in the Wave Rebellion Pro 2, but its geometry is the problem for many: sore legs and calves, and a heel taper that did not work.
Runners describe the Cloudmonster 2 as very cushioned with a roomy toe box. A couple who loved the original find it squishier and less lively.
Runners find the Adizero EVO SL ATR more stable than the regular EVO SL, but heavier and a bit slower. It suits roads and non-technical trails better than technical ground.
Runners mostly love the Supernova Prima 2 for its soft, bouncy and comfortable ride. A couple see it as an everyday comfort shoe that feels sluggish rather than a performance shoe.

Trail runners find the Agravic Speed Ultra 2 comfortable and stable, a clear improvement on the first version, and it holds up over long distances. It is fine on rocky ground, though not the best there.
Runners most often mention the VIA Olympus 2's arch shape, which bothers several, though one says it faded after about 30 km. It is firm, but softer than the original.
Runners mostly find the Novablast 6 stable and cushioned with some snap. One hated it for lacking the spring of the 5.
Trail runners find the Trabuco Max 3 soft yet bouncy, stable and very grippy. A snug toe box bothered one.
Trail runners like the Catamount 3 as a light, nimble and comfortable shoe with good traction, toe room and ground feel. One wants something comfier for long distances.
Runners find the Challenger 8 holds up well, with several getting hundreds of kilometers from a pair, and they see it as a solid successor to the 7. One fell apart after two months of light use.
Runners mostly use the Clifton PRO as a comfortable easy-day or warm-up shoe with a bouncy feel. A couple would not choose it for faster running or could not find a place for it.
Runners find the Mach X 3 snappy, protective and bouncy, good as a daily trainer and for faster efforts. Heel slip and slight extra weight were mentioned by one.
Runners find the Rincon 3 light and responsive for easy running. Several report the midsole fading after a few hundred miles, though others get much longer from a pair.
Runners mostly like the 1080 v15's plush, bouncy and responsive ride, better than the older Fresh Foam. One returned it because the thick upper is not breathable.
Runners find the More Trail v3 a good fit for mixed road and trail running, with cushioning and comfort for long runs.
Runners find the SuperComp Elite v5 a comfortable, protective race shoe that suits half and full marathon distances.
Trail runners find the Terra Kiger 9 comfortable and cushioned, and several get many kilometers from a pair. Grip is described as okay to good.
Runners find the Vaporfly 4 light, snappy and propulsive. Reactions to the upper are mixed.
Runners report an insole that slips and a toe box that sits very low. One beginner has put over 500 km into a pair with little wear.
Trail runners like the Xodus Ultra 4's cushioning and comfort, but two had blisters or severe foot pain on longer, technical efforts.
